title: Operational playbook for live-sampled verification, decay detection, and pin heuristics for published performance profiles
creator: Sophia Chen
description:
Goal: Produce an operational playbook and automation checklist for publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles that combines (1) live-sampled verification from shadow/replica traffic, (2) automated decay detection and scheduled refresh, and (3) deterministic pinning heuristics for model version selection. This document will be the canonical runbook for PMs, runtime engineers, and on-call SREs to: publish a new profile, validate it against production signals, decide pin/unpin actions, and retire stale profiles with minimal customer disruption.

Why this work: We currently publish verified performance profiles from offline benchmarks and sampled synthetic load. These profiles are critical for routing, cost estimations, and autoscaling. However, model characteristics drift in production (latency regresses under realistic request distributions; KV cache hit patterns change; throughput variance appears on some hardware). Without a live verification loop and clear pin heuristics, teams either over-pin (blocking rollouts) or under-pin (risking regressions). This playbook aims to close that gap and reduce manual triage by formalizing thresholds, telemetry, and automated remediation suggestions.

Scope and success metrics:
- Build a written playbook and automation checklist covering publishing -> 72-hour shadow verification -> pin/unpin decision -> scheduled refresh/archival.
- Automate sampling and verification pipelines so newly published profiles receive a 72-hour live validation run with shadow traffic within 24 hours of publication.
- Define decay detection rules to surface profiles whose latency or cost has drifted beyond tolerance within 30 days.
- Reduce manual rollback/incident tasks tied to profile mismatches by 60% in the next quarter.

Key constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Sampling overhead vs fidelity: Shadowing real traffic provides best fidelity but increases infra cost. We will sample at a configurable rate (default 0.5% of traffic per model anchor) and limit to peak-hour window variants to reduce cost while preserving signal.
- False positives from noisy telemetry: We will combine multiple signals (p50/p95 latency, normalized cost-per-token, throughput stability, KV cache hit-rate delta) and require at least two orthogonal triggers for automated alerts.
- Pin permanence vs agility: Pinned profiles prevent automatic model variant substitution and preserve customer expectations, but can slow beneficial rollouts. Pin decisions will have TTLs (default 14 days) and auto-review reminders to ensure agility.

Playbook outline (high level):
1) Pre-publish checklist (owner: PM)
   - PRD or model onboarding doc linked; profile metadata filled (sequence-length anchor, hw target, sample harness seed).
   - Offline benchmarks uploaded (latency/throughput/cost normalized) and signed artifact created.
   - Risk review done if changes involve quantization, sparse variants, or breaking tokenizer changes.
2) Publish step (owner: Runtime on-call / Release engineer)
   - Publish profile to performance-catalog (signed manifest + provenance).
   - Trigger shadow verification job and record expected baselines.
3) 72-hour live verification (owner: Runtime team automation)
   - Shadow at default 0.5% sample of production traffic for 72 hours across representative regions.
   - Capture the following: p50/p95 latency, token-level cost, throughput per GPU, KV cache hit-rate, memory pressure, OOM logs.
   - Normalize results to baseline x86/hw baseline and compute drift ratios.
   - Flag if (A) p95 latency increases > 1.35x AND (B) cost-per-token increases > 1.20x OR (C) throughput drops > 20%.
4) Pin heuristics and TTLs (owner: PM + Runtime)
   - If verification passes within thresholds, profile is eligible for auto-pin for 14 days. Auto-pin is a soft-pin: routing honors profile but admin can opt out.
   - If verification shows minor drift (p95 1.10–1.35x), create a canary cohort (5% traffic) with auto-observation for 48h and require PM review.
   - Major drift triggers automatic deprecation notice and rollback workflow.
5) Decay detection and scheduled refresh
   - Background job computes rolling 30-day staleness score from production telemetry and synthetic checks. Score > 0.7 triggers a refresh playbook.
   - For high-usage models, refresh cadence defaults to 14 days; for low-usage to 60 days.
6) Deprecation and archival
   - Profiles with no successful verification and low usage after 90 days are archived. Archive process removes routing recommendations but retains signed artifact and audit log.

Acceptance criteria:
- PM-verified playbook doc published in Confluence with step-by-step commands and links.
- Automation pipeline in CI/CD that runs a 72-hour shadow verification within 24 hours of a profile publish.
- Dashboards (Console) exist for: live-verification status, staleness score heatmap, per-profile drift history, and current pin state.
- Runbook contains explicit rollback criteria and a PR template for emergency profile unpublish.

Risks and mitigation:
- Cost blowup from shadowing: use capped sampling and regional caps. Track cost per shadow run and add budget alerts.
- Insufficient signal for low-volume models: combine synthetic load injection with shadowing and increase sampling windows.
- Human ops burden: automate summary emails, generate suggested actions, and provide one-click unpin/unpublish in Console.

Next steps / short-term plan (first 3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: Draft Confluence playbook; implement signed-manifest publish hook; create dashboard mocks (PM + Design).
- Sprint 2: Implement shadowing scheduler and telemetry aggregator; wire alerts for the two-signal rule.
- Sprint 3: Implement auto-pin TTL, canary cohort tooling, and archival job; run pilot on 3 medium-traffic models.

Longer term (Q2+):
- Integrate with RBAC and audit logs for enterprise customers.
- Surface cost-normalized recommendations in Console and expose per-profile rollback buttons.
- Study ML-driven profile refresh suggestions using drift predictors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook published to Confluence and linked from performance-catalog UI; 2) Automation triggers a 72-hour verification within 24h of publish in staging; 3) Dashboard tiles for verification status, staleness score, and pin state visible to PM/Runtime teams; 4) Pilot executed on 3 models and results logged; 5) TTL-based auto-pin implemented with manual override
